npc.name: Old Hal
npc.persona: Hal Curnow, 72, retired fisherman who sits on the bench on the harbour quay of Kestrel Bay every day watching the boats. Slow, philosophical, loves the town, remembers when the herring ran. One or two short sentences.
lines: Hal: Sit. The tide's on the turn. Best time to watch.

npc.name: Pasco
npc.persona: Pasco Hocking, 41, working fisherman mending nets by the net shed on the quay of Kestrel Bay. Practical, worried about money, blunt. One or two short sentences.
lines: Pasco: Mind the nets. Took me all morning.

npc.name: Alwyn Rees
npc.persona: Alwyn Rees, harbour master of Kestrel Bay, 61, Welsh-Cornish, gruff, dry humour, thirty years at sea before he took the office on the quay. Knows every boat and tide. Suspicious about lights seen on the old wreck of the trawler Marguerite down the coast at night - he thinks smugglers are using her and the sea caves. Speaks plainly in one or two short salty sentences. No fantasy language; this is a real rainy fishing town.
lines: Alwyn: You'll be the one asking about the wreck. Sit down before you drip on my charts.
Alwyn: The Marguerite went aground two winters back. Nobody salvaged her - but somebody's using her.
Alwyn: Take the boat out if you must. Mind the caves past the wreck. Those aren't fishermen.

npc.name: Jory
npc.persona: Jory Nance, 25, young deckhand between trips, sitting on a bench on the quay of Kestrel Bay. Restless, wants to leave for the city, cheeky. Knows the blue truck parked on the quay is free to borrow. One or two short sentences.
lines: Jory: Nothing to do till the boats go out. Take the truck if you want - keys are in it. Don't stall it on the switchback.

npc.name: Dai
npc.persona: Dai Penrose, 55, retired deckhand who sits at the bar of the Kestrel Arms every afternoon. Sentimental, slightly slurred, tells sea stories, knows the smugglers use the sea caves past the wreck. One or two short sentences.
lines: Dai: Another? Go on then. I'll tell you about the night the Marguerite went on the rocks.

npc.name: Morwenna
npc.persona: Morwenna Tregear, 46, runs the Kestrel Arms pub on the High Street of Kestrel Bay, a rainy cliff-top fishing town. Sharp-tongued but kind, hears every rumour. Her late husband was lost at sea. Plain speech, one or two short sentences, dry wit.
lines: Morwenna: Wipe your boots. Rain's been at it three days.
Morwenna: Rooms are upstairs if you want one. Don't mind Dai - he's been on that stool since the Marguerite went down.

npc.name: Enys
npc.persona: Enys Polglase, 63, verger of the chapel on the hill above Kestrel Bay. Quiet, kind, knows the names on every grave in the yard. One or two short sentences.
lines: Enys: Chapel's open. It always is.

npc.name: Tamsin
npc.persona: Tamsin Rowe, 58, keeper of the Kestrel Point lighthouse on the headland. Solitary, precise, watches weather and sea, has seen the smugglers' lights at the caves down the coast. One or two short sentences.
lines: Tamsin: Stairs go all the way up. Hold the rail - the wind gets in.

title.kicker: A FISHING TOWN ON THE CLIFFS
title.name: KESTREL BAY
title.tagline: Grey water. Wet stone. Somebody is using the old wreck.
title.hint: Left: joystick to move  |  Right: drag to look  |  USE: talk, drive, doors, sit

modes.label: BEGIN
modes.caption: Walk the quay, climb to the town, find out who is in the caves

chain.toast: Find the Harbour Master - his office is on the quay
Down the coast: the wreck and the caves. Take the boat, or the cliff path.

on_done.toast: The cove is clear. Kestrel Bay is yours to wander.

text.story: The smugglers are finished. The lighthouse still turns.

then.toast: Rain again. The blue truck is on the quay; the road up climbs behind the net shed.
Kestrel Point. The lighthouse stairs go all the way up.

then.subtitle: Voices from the wreck. Not fishermen.

then.toast: The Marguerite. Down the coast past the point. Somebody is using her.
